text:
Srinivas: Heads-up — noticed a recurring pattern in eu-west this morning: autoscaler adds nodes but headroom still goes negative in the same pool, and p90 tail latency spikes. Feels like an AZ-local hotpath where pods are getting scheduled in a different AZ and network egress/batch window widens. See provisional queries below, looking for quick sanity check before I add panels to Grafana.

Olivia: ugh, saw a couple of these too. did an ad-hoc correlate with recent deploy? could be a taint/toleration mismatch causing pods to avoid some nodes.

Srinivas: nope, no deploys in that window. cluster-autoscaler logs show scale up, but kube-scheduler shows pods pending while nodes are initializing in another AZ. suspect scheduling anti-affinity + node labeling subtlety.

Alex: can you paste the promql you're using?

Srinivas: sure — quick ones I used: 
```# per-pool headroom (tokens/sec headroom per pool)
(sum(rate(inference_request_tokens_total[1m])) by (pool) * 1) - (sum(kube_node_status_capacity{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"}) by (pool) * ideal_throughput_per_gpu)
\n# observed avg batch size per model
avg by(model) (rate(inference_batch_size_sum[1m]) / rate(inference_batch_size_count[1m]))
\n# kv cache hit ratio per pool
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) by (pool) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])) by (pool)```
These are rough; want a panel that shows per-AZ headroom heatmap and a per-pool "observed vs expected nodes" ratio.

Tara: agree on heatmap. also add "batch-window width": the observed average time between first token and last token in a burst — that's where cross-AZ egress shows up. promql: 
```histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_batch_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool, az))```

Noah: fwiw, I saw a config where kube-scheduler's topologySpread constraints were applied too strictly for a couple of pools; pods prefer different AZs and autoscaler thinks "we added capacity" while scheduling still constrained. Not necessarily a scaling bug, more a topology policy mismatch.

Srinivas: interesting — that could explain it. adding a diagnostic panel: "scheduling failures / reason" scraped from kube events and aggregated by pool/az.

Olivia: +1. also recommend we relax the existing static queue-depth alert. It's firing too often. Instead: alert on the ratio of queue_depth to per-pod headroom (i.e., normalized queue pressure). Example: 
```
alert: HighQueuePressure
expr: (sum(inference_queue_depth) by (pool) / (sum(kube_node_status_capacity{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"}) by (pool) * expected_tokens_per_gpu)) > 0.7
for: 3m
```
This should reduce noise and scale with pool size.

oncall-bot: ALERT fired: HighQueuePressure on pool=eu-west-gpu-pool at 1976543225. Triggered rules: HighQueuePressure.

Srinivas: saw that. oncall copy: @Olivia can you take primary on the dashboard and alert change? I'll add the headroom heatmap + scheduling-failure panel.

Olivia: taking. I'll spin up a temp dashboard and post a link. plan: add panels — per-az headroom heatmap, batch-window p95, kv cache hit ratio, scheduler-failure counts, observed/expected node ratio.

Alex: we should also surface the cost signal. add a "burst vs reserved utilization" panel: fraction of tokens served by burst nodes vs reserved. helps product teams evaluate reserving more capacity.

Tara: quick ops playbook note: if headroom goes negative and all AZs show uneven utilization, prefer draining the hottest AZ's pods (move traffic) before adding permanent reserved capacity. saves cost.

Noah: action items:
- Olivia: create dashboard + update alert (ETA 2h)
- Srinivas: add promql + kube-events scraping for scheduler-failure reasons (ETA 4h)
- Alex: add cost split panel (ETA EOD)
- Tara: draft ops runbook snippet for hotpath mitigation (ETA EOD)

Olivia: starting now. will post dashboard link in ~45m. tagging @Noah for help with kube-events exporter if needed. :rocket:

Srinivas: thanks — after we have dashboards let's run a small chaos test (reschedule pods between AZs) to ensure alert sensitivity is correct.

oncall-bot: NOTE: incident timeline event recorded at 1976543270.

Olivia: posted temp dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/dash/abc123/eu-hotpath-headroom (will iterate). Initial tweak: changed HighQueuePressure to use per-pool normalization. monitor -> will revert if noisy.

Alex: looks good. caught one oddity: eu-west-gpu-pool had a stale node label `zone=eu-west-1a-old` which the scheduler ignored. cleaned it up.

Tara: nice catch. little things like that bite often.

Noah: closing loop — once dashboards stabilize let's add an annotation on the SLO board and a small regression test in infra-evals for per-az scheduling policies.

Srinivas: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a PR for the kube-events metrics and an outline for the chaos test.
